thread_analysis.thread_summary: Teraoka Seiko Co., Ltd. (contact Hideaki Haraguchi) continues its long-running Bluetooth certification relationship with Allion (Masaya Iida, Itsuo Sakai), covering a new Espressif-module-based registration (requiring a Host+Controller Subsystem Multi-Design combination since the module isn't Component-registered, following the same pattern documented in thread_0247/thread_0264) through to Compliance Folder delivery, plus a distinct post-certification question about changing a Service UUID from 16-bit standard to 128-bit custom format.
all_questions_found: Does switching a Service UUID from 16-bit standard to 128-bit custom affect existing SIG certification, and is a change application needed? (see thread_0019_case_01)

(Already documented pattern, see thread_0247/thread_0264) Why does this module require a Host+Controller Subsystem Multi-Design combination rather than a simple Component reference, and why is the registration support fee higher as a result?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Beyond the duplicated module-registration-structure content (see thread_0247 and thread_0264 for that pattern), this thread's new contribution clarifies that switching a Service UUID to 128-bit custom format reclassifies the profile as proprietary, removing any SIG declaration or testing obligation for that change.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0019_case_01 for the new decision logic; the module registration structure content follows the same logic already documented in thread_0247 and thread_0264.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: This thread adds a useful precedent to the established Teraoka Seiko relationship: post-certification Service UUID format changes (16-bit standard to 128-bit custom) require no SIG action at all, since they reclassify the affected profile as proprietary — a question worth proactively addressing for any customer planning similar UUID changes on already-certified products.
